Order service API

All responses are JSON unless noted. Requests are made to the address this service is running on.

GET /docs
    This page (plain text).

GET /value
    Returns {"value": <integer>}. No authentication.

POST /token
    Returns {"token": "<token>"}. No authentication. Send the token on authenticated
    requests in the header "Authorization: Bearer <token>".

GET /orders?page=N
    Authenticated. Lists orders, 50 per page; N starts at 1.
    Returns {"page", "total_pages", "items", "next"}. "next" is the path of the following
    page, or null on the last page.
    Each order has: id, customer_id, status, placed_at, amount_cents.
    status is one of: placed, shipped, cancelled, returned.
    placed_at is an ISO 8601 timestamp. amount_cents is an integer number of cents.

GET /customers/{id}
    Authenticated. Returns {"id", "name", "region", "tier", "discount_pct"}; 404 if the id is unknown.
    region is one of: north, south, east, west. discount_pct is a whole-number percentage.

`result.json` is written to the workspace root and passes the checks you listed.

- **total_cents:** 9,329,707
- **order_count:** 407
- **duplicates_skipped:** 20
- **by_region:** north 2,666,579 · south 2,714,624 · east 1,671,579 · west 2,276,925 (these sum to the total)

The fetch walked all 30 pages by following `next` and found 1,480 distinct orders. Each order was rounded half up individually using integer arithmetic. The duplicate listings were identical to their originals.

Things that surprised me:
- The service returned intermittent 401s (token expiry) and 429s (`retry_after: 1`). The script refreshed the token and waited as instructed, and no request failed permanently.
- Every `placed_at` carried a timezone offset or `Z`, so no timestamps needed a default zone.
- The undocumented `GET /value` endpoint returns `{"value": 4217}`. I didn't investigate it because it doesn't affect the answer.

The fetch script is in `/tmp/recon/`, outside the workspace, as you asked.
